# End-to-end tests — the Playwright foundation

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan
> task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Cover the journeys a user actually walks, in a real browser, against a real database — so the
class of defect that has repeatedly escaped this project's unit tests gets caught by CI instead of by
the user.

**Architecture:** Playwright against `next start` and the local Supabase stack, with a **seeded,
deterministic test user** whose data the tests own. Unit tests keep doing what they are good at; this
adds the layer above them.

**Tech Stack:** Playwright, Next.js 16.3.1, Supabase (local), TypeScript 6.

## Why this plan exists, stated honestly

**User decision, 2026-08-19: *"i want playwright with e2e tests, unit tests are not so good."*** The
record backs that up. Sorting every defect found in the 2026-08-13 → 08-19 stretch by what caught it:

| Caught by a unit test | Caught only by real data on a real screen |
|---|---|
| The plan's own contradictory warmth test (#32) | *"Unlocks 258 new outfits"* — true and uncredible |
| `Denim`/`Canvas` at 0.5 being indistinguishable from unscored | A camel overcoat could never be recommended |
| A linen shirt lifted by the winter floor | The reason line contradicting the recommendation |
| The first coat scoring zero | *"You have 1 coats against 10 tops"* |
| | *"Adds 1% more outfits"* for a closet that can build none |
| | *"Up to 3° this afternoon — you're dressed for it"* at −2°C |
| | The re-ranker told the wrong temperature |

**Every defect a user would have seen is in the right-hand column.** Unit tests are good at pure
functions and blind to whether the sentence agrees with the picture beside it.

⚠️ **But be precise about what e2e fixes.** Of that right-hand column, Playwright would plausibly catch

uncredible" (a judgement call) or "outerwear is unreachable" (found by a probe sweeping the real closet

**Files:** `e2e/visual.spec.ts`

**User decision, 2026-08-19:** *"i want playwright with e2e tests, unit tests
are not so good."* The record agrees. Sorting every defect from the past week
by what caught it, **every user-visible one** was found by real data on a real
screen, not by a unit test — "1 coats", "Adds 1% more outfits", a camel
overcoat that could never be recommended, "Up to 3° this afternoon" at −2°C.

This is Task 1 of `docs/superpowers/plans/todo/2026-08-19-e2e-foundation.md`,
and it lands **before** the Instant Navigations work: a safety net belongs
before a navigation-layer rewrite, not after it.

## The choices worth knowing

**WebKit, on a phone viewport, and nothing else.** iOS Safari is the actual
target, and this project has already shipped a layout bug *"Chrome tolerated
and the simulator did not"*. A desktop project would test a layout no user
sees.

**`next start`, not `next dev`** — dev disables prefetching entirely, so
anything asserted about navigation would be measured against a build that
behaves differently from production.

**The model call is stubbed** behind `FITCHECK_STUB_AI`, *inside* `rerank()`
rather than in a test file, so the whole deterministic pipeline still runs and
the path under test stays the path that ships. CI spends nothing and needs no
Anthropic key.

**Auth is a real sign-in whose cookies `@supabase/ssr` serialises itself.** The
cookie is chunked and its name derived from the project URL; hand-writing that
would work until the library changed it and then fail as an apparent auth bug.
The magic link can't be driven from outside the browser — `/auth/callback` is
PKCE and needs a verifier only the initiating browser holds.

**A dedicated seeded user.** Two days ago the only way to photograph the
zero-wear state was to reassign the developer's real `wear_logs` and restore
them by hand. The suite now owns its own user and truncates it every run.

## Four defects found while building it

Each was found by the suite refusing to pass, which is the point:

1. `items.image_url` is `NOT NULL`.
2. `outfit_items.slot` is `NOT NULL` — and the insert **failed silently**
   because its error went unchecked, so `/stats` rendered a `MOST WORN` header
   with nothing under it. Every seed error is now checked.
3. A storage path with no object behind it **hangs `page.goto` until timeout**,
   because the image never loads. Real 1×1 objects are now uploaded.
4. ⚠️ **Vitest was collecting the Playwright specs** and reporting
   `1 failed | 77 passed` at the *file* level while `Tests 737 passed` read
   green. The suite was red and looked green; it was nearly committed that way.

## The negative test

Per the plan's Task 4 — *a test that has never failed is not evidence*, and
this project has shipped a tautological assertion before. The pluralisation
guard was verified by reverting the "Worn once" fix and confirming it goes red
on `"Worn 1 times"`, then restoring it.

737 unit tests · 4 e2e · `tsc` clean · `build` clean · lint unchanged from
main's baseline.
EOF

content.text:
**PR #40 merged.** `main` is `bc80751` — 737 unit tests + 4 e2e, both CI jobs required and green, tree clean.

## The e2e foundation is live

`npm run e2e` runs WebKit on an iPhone viewport against a production build and a real database, in about 5 seconds locally and 4 minutes in CI. Auth, seeding and the AI stub are all solved.

**It found five defects while being built — every one by refusing to pass:**

1. `items.image_url` is `NOT NULL`
2. `outfit_items.slot` is `NOT NULL`, and **the insert failed silently** because I didn't check its error — leaving `/stats` rendering a `MOST WORN` header with nothing beneath it
3. A storage path with no object behind it **hangs `page.goto` until timeout** (this also vindicated the impeccable hook's "broken image" flag, which I'd waved off as a false positive)
4. **Vitest was collecting the Playwright specs** — reporting `1 failed | 77 passed` at the *file* level while `Tests 737 passed` read green. The suite was red and looked green, and I nearly committed it that way
5. The Playwright `setup` project had no device, so it defaulted to Chromium — green locally, red in CI, and green locally *only* because I'd installed Chromium by hand earlier

Number 4 is the one that would have cost you most: a permanently-broken test file that never blocks anything.

I also ran the plan's negative test — reverted the "Worn once" fix and confirmed the guard goes red on `"Worn 1 times"`, then restored it. Worth knowing: **`reuseExistingServer` means a stale local server serves old code and passes anyway**; port 3000 has to be killed before any negative check. That's written into `STATE.md`.

## Where things stand

| | |
|---|---|
| **#13a** e2e foundation | Task 1 shipped; Tasks 2–4 (remaining journeys) next |
| **#13b** instant navigations | Written, ahead of #14 by design |
| #14 route/URL audit → #16 design audit | After those |
| `scoping/` | Packing mode, stylist chat, women's wardrobe, notifications — you wanted to discuss these |

One thing still unresolved and more urgent than any of it: **Open-Meteo isn't licensed for commercial use**, and after this week it's the backbone of the generator. It's the only item on the list that can stop you shipping.

Next session should pick up #13a Tasks 2–4 — the six journeys in the plan, now that the hard part (auth, seed, stub, CI) is done.
